set.descent_text: Ultramega OK has no independent, well-established rappel line of its own — it is a Northeast Buttress route whose last pitch finishes up an offwidth crack to the summit, though a party that loses the line high up can traverse ledges into upper North Face terrain (near Burgundy Ledge) and finish from there. From wherever the route is topped out, the standard way down is the North Face's 5-rappel descent: ~40m from a heavily slung summit boulder down the middle of the upper face to a bolted ledge anchor; ~55m from the bolts down lichen-covered rock to a huge ledge near a rock arch (traverse the ledge to a constriction with slings); ~55m from that constriction down to a blue-slung horn; ~40m from the horn to broad scree ledges (watch the rope pull here — lots of snag potential); and a final ~60m to the base of the first-pitch chimney, near where Action Potential and the North Face start. Double 60m ropes make this clean; parties with a single 70m have reported getting down with some downclimbing between stances, but it's tighter on this line than on the standard North Face. From the base of the raps, reverse the Burgundy Col approach back to the highway. A few parties describe instead downclimbing loose 3rd/4th-class terrain on Burgundy's east side back toward the col to avoid rappelling altogether, but this is opportunistic route-finding rather than an established descent, and is not recommended in the wet or for parties unfamiliar with the terrain.

set.overview: Pandora's Box (also called the W Couloir) is the standard moderate couloir linking Colchuck and Dragontail near Colchuck Col. It's a west-facing snow/talus couloir a couple hundred feet east of Colchuck Col, most often climbed as the summit finish for Dragontail Peak via the Colchuck Glacier approach. The couloir is class 3 scrambling with sections of steep snow up to roughly 40-45°; it is not a technical ice or mixed climb. A single ice axe, crampons, and comfort on steep snow/talus are the normal kit.
set.descent_text: From the top of the couloir/Pandora's Box, descend left and traverse northeast to the true summit (some parties rope up for this exposed traverse), or alternatively exit about 30 ft below the notch, scramble Class 4 rock roughly 20 ft, and follow the ridge left to the top. From the summit, the standard descent is southeast to a saddle, then east across a long snow slope to Aasgard Pass, then down the pass's steep talus/snow (~2,200 ft in under a mile) to Colchuck Lake - stay climbers' left near the granite walls and beware drifting climbers' right into cliffs near Colchuck Peak. Crampons/axe are recommended into mid-summer; early season the descent can largely be glissaded. No rappels are needed on this standard summit-and-Aasgard-Pass finish. If a party instead retreats directly back down the couloir rather than topping out, downclimbing steep snow/ice or building an improvised rappel off natural gear (slung chockstones or horns) in the couloir could become necessary - this specific scenario is not recorded anywhere but is a reasonable contingency to plan for in a steep snow couloir.

set.approach: The Wilson Glacier sits on the east side of Mount Adams, descending from around 10,600 ft to a terminus near 7,400 ft — a less-visited, less-documented flank than the standard south or north-side routes. Parties reach it via the Cold Springs/South Climb trailhead (5,600 ft, FS Rd 8040 off FS Rd 80): follow the South Climb Trail #183 about 1 mile up an old road bed to the junction with the Round the Mountain Trail, then instead of continuing north toward Lunch Counter, follow Round the Mountain Trail east below Crescent Glacier onto Yakama Nation land, where a separate tribal permit is required and the trail ends at Hellroaring Canyon; the way on, north around the mountain's eastern flank toward the Wilson/Klickitat glacier basins, is a long off-trail traverse with route-finding, creek crossings, and exposure to rockfall directly below the headwall's cliff bands. Given the route's distance (~27 km) and gain (6,700 ft) roughly match the other long approach routes on this mountain, expect a full day just to reach a camp near the toe of the Wilson Glacier before a summit attempt.

findings.claim: approach: follow the Round the Mountain Trail 'east and then north ... around the mountain's eastern flank' toward the Wilson/Klickitat basins
findings.evidence: The Forest Service maintains Trail #9 only to the reservation boundary. East of it the trail runs through Bird Creek Meadows under Yakama Nation management and ends on a reservation road at the western edge of Hellroaring Canyon. It never goes north around the east flank; the trail system leaves a gap on the east side. A separate Yakama Nation permit is required on reservation land, and the Bird Creek Meadows section has been closed for years (closed after the 2015 fire, listed as closed indefinitely). The Wilson Glacier is on the east slopes, on the reservation side. The sentence is corrected to where the trail really ends and to the permit requirement; the rest is kept.

findings.claim: Whether non-members may travel off-trail on the reservation's east flank at all
findings.evidence: No source found states the rule for travel beyond the Mount Adams Recreation Area. A human should confirm current Yakama Nation access before this approach is presented as usable.
